## Goal

As an operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`, I want the CPU and I/O stall-pressure thresholds to reflect real PSI stall data now that `/proc/pressure` parsing works, so the pressure diagnosis fires on genuine contention instead of staying green until the host is near-dead.

## Problem statement

`cpu_pressure` (warning 70 / critical 85, `some` avg10) and `io_pressure` (warning 50 / critical 80, `full` avg10) were inherited from the pre-parser-fix configuration and have never been validated against real stall data. The IO threshold is worse than unvalidated: a 50 % `full`-line stall is effectively never reached, so `io_pressure` stays permanently green even under genuine I/O starvation — the exact signal the PSI work (SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW) was meant to surface.

## Users

- **Operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`** — "As an operator, I want the before-table pressure rows to flag real CPU contention and I/O starvation at levels my multi-agent host actually reaches, so I am told about a problem while it is still actionable."
- **Agent triaging a slow host** — "As an agent, I want `analyze_pressures()` to surface an actionable pressure with contributors when the host is genuinely starved, instead of skipping a permanently-green `io_pressure` row."
- **Skill maintainer** — "As a maintainer, I want the calibrated values consistent across `config.yaml`, `config.py::_DEFAULTS` and `SKILL.md`, with boundary tests, so a future parser change cannot silently re-introduce the silence."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — `cpu_pressure` is calibrated to **warning 30 / critical 60** (`some` avg10) and `io_pressure` to **warning 5 / critical 20** (`full` avg10) in `config.yaml` and `config.py::_DEFAULTS`, mirroring the `memory_pressure` full-line calibration for IO.
- **AC2** — Calibration is validated against real stall data: the archived busy-host observations (CPU `some` avg10 = 11.58 at load 11.92 on 16 cores → `low`; CPU `some` avg10 = 88.78 at load ~44 → `critical`) classify as expected, and **at least one bounded controlled I/O-stall sample** is captured (e.g. a short `dd`/write burst) showing a numeric IO `full` value that currently stays green under 50/80, with the sample and classification recorded in a comment on this item.
- **AC3** — Unit tests cover the new classification boundaries for both metrics: cpu `some` 29.9 → `low`, 30.0 → `warning`, 60.0 → `critical`; io `full` 4.9 → `low`, 5.0 → `warning`, 20.0 → `critical` — replacing the old 70/85 and 50/80 boundary assertions.
- **AC4** — `config.yaml` comments and `SKILL.md` document the new values, their `some`/`full` line basis, the observed-data provenance (including the induced IO sample), and why the IO warning never fired under 50/80. `SKILL.md`'s "Threshold provenance" paragraph is updated to state the validated values rather than "not yet validated".
- **AC5** — All related documentation in this repository is updated: `config.yaml` comments, `config.py` docstrings/comments, `SKILL.md` metric table and provenance section, plus any code comments in `metrics.py` that reference the thresholds. This skill has no README or docs-site entry, so no other documentation surface needs an update.
- **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — calibration basis:** the archived samples (11.58 busy / 88.78 extreme) plus one induced IO sample bracket realistic stall ranges on this 16-core multi-agent host; other hosts (fewer/more cores, different workloads) can still override per-host values in `config.yaml`.
- **Risk — false amber at 30 % CPU `some`-stall:** a heavily loaded-but-healthy multi-agent host can briefly cross 30 % `some` (at least one task stalled) during test-suite bursts; acceptable — it is the honest stall signal, and `some` semantics are designed to fire early.
- **Risk — induced IO sample disturbs the live host:** the bounded burst must be short and small (e.g. a few hundred MB write/read) so it does not itself cause a false-positive pressure reading on a busy host; time it outside the brief write window.
- **Risk — doc drift:** three surfaces (`config.yaml`, `config.py::_DEFAULTS`, `SKILL.md`) must stay in lock-step; AC4/AC5 and the existing `test_shipped_config_matches_defaults` guard this.
- **Scope-creep risk:** adjacent recalibration ideas (e.g. load-average multipliers vs. PSI, per-host dynamic thresholds) are recorded as linked work items, not folded into this item.

## Impact

Operators now get honest CPU and I/O stall alarms at levels a real multi-agent host reaches — CPU contention flagged at 30 % `some`-stall and genuine I/O starvation at 5 % `full`-stall — instead of a metric that stays green until the box is thrashing.

## Constraints

- **Scope:** threshold values + consistent config/docs/tests + one bounded controlled I/O-stall sample for validation. No parser, line-selection, metric-key, or action behaviour changes.
- **Stable metric keys:** `cpu_pressure` / `io_pressure` must not change (consumed by `pressure_analysis._PRESSURE_METRICS` and the before/after table).
- **Classification semantics:** `classify_metric` is inclusive at the warning/critical lower bounds (`value >= critical` → critical, `value >= warning` → warning); boundary tests assert exactly those edges.
- **Line bases unchanged:** cpu → `some`, io → `full` (decided in SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW); no fallback on missing lines.
- **No new dependencies**; stdlib/unittest only.
- **Repo boundary:** changes land in `skill/machine-hygiene` in this repo (worktree), never the installed global copy by hand.

## Existing state

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py::_DEFAULTS` — `cpu_pressure: warning 70 / critical 85`; `io_pressure: warning 50 / critical 80`.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/config.yaml` — same values, with comments claiming ">70 % indicates moderate CPU contention" (70 % `some`-stall is far past moderate) and ">50 % I/O stalled — noticeable slowdown" (never reached on `full`).
- `skill/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — "Threshold provenance" says cpu/io thresholds "have not yet been validated against real stall data".
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_config.py` — asserts the 70/85 and 50/80 defaults and file-override behaviour.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_metrics.py` — `test_cpu_pressure_boundaries` (69.9/70/85) and `test_io_pressure_boundaries` (49.9/50/80) lock in the old values.
- Real observed data: CPU `some` avg10 = 88.78 (2026-09-27, load ~44/16 cores) and 11.58 (2026-10-21 discovery, load 11.92); IO `full` avg10 = 0.00–0.05 (idle observations only — no busy IO sample yet).

## Desired change

1. `_DEFAULTS` and `config.yaml`: `cpu_pressure` → 30/60 (`some` avg10); `io_pressure` → 5/20 (`full` avg10, mirroring `memory_pressure`).
2. Update comments: cpu description corrected to "(moderate CPU contention)" at 30 %; io description explains `full`-line stall % semantics and that 50/80 never fired.
3. Update `SKILL.md` provenance paragraph with the calibrated values, the archived and induced sample evidence, and the rationale.
4. Update boundary tests in `test_metrics.py` and default tests in `test_config.py` to the new values.
5. Validation run: capture a bounded controlled I/O-stall sample (write/read burst, a few seconds), render the `io_pressure` classification under the new thresholds, and paste the sample + classification into a comment on this item.

## Key Files

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py` — `_DEFAULTS` cpu_pressure/io_pressure values (and any threshold-referencing comments).
- `skill/machine-hygiene/config.yaml` — cpu_pressure/io_pressure blocks, warning/critical values and explaining comments.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — "Threshold provenance" paragraph and any metric-table threshold notes.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_config.py` — default-value and file-override assertions for cpu/io pressure.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_metrics.py` — `test_cpu_pressure_boundaries`, `test_io_pressure_boundaries` and the `collect_metrics` pressure assertions.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW** (completed) — PSI parser fix; this item's `discovered-from` source; established `some`/`full` line selection and the `memory_pressure` 5/20 calibration precedent.
- **WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY** (ContextHub, completed) — threshold miscalibration for multi-agent hosts (process/thread/swap); adjacent calibration work, shipped.
- **WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ** (ContextHub, open) — duplicate proposed-actions table/actions; same discovery session, independent defect.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: `cpu_pressure` calibration target (`some` avg10)?**
  - Options: (A) keep 70/85, validate + document; (B) lower to warn 30 / crit 60 to catch contention earlier; (C) middle ground (warn 50 / crit 75).
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **B**. **Recommended:** B — 70 % `some`-stall means the host is already severely degraded; an amber band from ~30 % lets the skill propose renice/kill remediation while the host is still responsive.
  - Evidence: real CPU `some` avg10 samples of 11.58 (busy, load 11.92) and 88.78 (extreme, load ~44) on 16-core hosts; current 70/85 classifies the former `low` and the latter `critical`.
- **Q2: `io_pressure` calibration target (`full` avg10)?**
  - Options: (A) mirror memory_pressure warn 5 / crit 20 (same full-line semantics); (B) slightly higher (10/30); (C) keep 50/80 but document.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **A**. **Recommended:** A — identical `full`-line semantics and an established 5/20 precedent; keeps the genuine I/O-starvation signal without false alarms at idle.
  - Evidence: observed IO `full` avg10 values are 0.00–0.05; 50/80 was never reachable so the metric stayed green under genuine I/O starvation.
- **Q3: validation data sufficiency (AC1)?**
  - Options: (A) archive observations + live `/proc/pressure` only; (B) also induce a bounded controlled I/O-stall sample.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **B**. **Recommended:** B — AC1 explicitly demands validation against observed busy-host stall percentages, and IO currently has zero busy samples; one bounded induced sample makes calibration evidence-based rather than assumed.
  - Evidence: no archived IO `full` sample exceeds 0.05; a short `dd`/write burst provides the missing busy data point.

No open questions remain.

# Fix `worklog_dir_flag` worktree resolution for worktrees under `<main>/.worklog/worktrees`

> **Provenance:** transferred from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT` (Tableau-Card-Engine
> store) by producer decision, where it was `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`
> (TCE worktree `wl-CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY-retire-legacy-choice-fields-and-the-clar`,
> commit `4975f6ff`), observed while running
> `render_report.py CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` from that worktree. The CG item is
> deleted after transfer; the full intake brief lives here.

## Problem statement

`shared/status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` builds ancestor candidates as
`parent / ".worklog"` for **every** parent, so when the cwd sits inside
`<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` the ancestor `<main>/.worklog`
itself yields `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`; it also accepts any `.worklog`
directory **without** checking that it is initialised. Both defects make
`worklog_dir_flag()` hand `wl` a store root that is either non-existent
(no-op flag) or uninitialised (`wl` fails with
`"Worklog system is not initialized"`), so skill scripts that shell out to
`wl` break when run from an `implement.py` worktree.

## Users

- **AI agent running skill scripts from an implement worktree** — `/skill:report`,
  `/skill:audit`, `persist_audit.py`, and status/lifecycle helpers all resolve
  the store through `worklog_dir_flag()` / `resolve_worklog_flags()`.
  Story: *As an agent finishing work in a worktree, `render_report.py <id>`
  must read the main checkout's worklog so my report is populated and my
  status transition is written to the store the producer reads.*
- **Producer / operator** — needs a trustworthy store resolution so a run from
  a worktree cannot silently target a wrong or uninitialised store.
  Story: *As the producer, when an agent reports from a worktree, the item it
  reports on must be the item in the main checkout's store, with no manual
  `--worklog-dir` correction.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs the resolution rule pinned by tests.
  Story: *As a skill maintainer, I need a regression test for the
  `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/…` layout so a future refactor of the ancestor
  walk cannot reintroduce a nested `.worklog/.worklog` path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves to the main checkout store.**
      With cwd = `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` and no `.worklog`
      in the worktree, `worklog_dir_flag()` returns
      `["--worklog-dir", "<main>/.worklog"]` (the initialised store), including
      when a stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC2 — no double suffix.** An ancestor directory already named
      `.worklog` is never extended to `.worklog/.worklog`; the worklog
      directory that is itself an ancestor is the candidate.
- [ ] **AC3 — initialised candidates only.** A candidate `.worklog` that is not
      initialised (`_is_initialized_worklog()` false — e.g. a worktree's
      committed `config.yaml`-only copy) is never returned; resolution
      continues to the nearest initialised ancestor, and returns `[]` (no flag)
      rather than an uninitialised path when nothing initialised exists.
- [ ] **AC4 — unit tests cover the worktree layouts.** New hermetic tests
      (tmp_path fixtures, no real `git worktree`, no network) covering:
      (a) `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` present;
      (b) a **subdirectory** of a worktree whose committed `.worklog/` holds
      only `config.yaml` (the uninitialised-candidate case);
      (c) a plain nested project cwd (no `.worklog` between cwd and the project
      root) still resolving as today (no regression).
- [ ] **AC5 — existing precedence preserved, no weakening.** Precedence
      `explicit --worklog-dir` > prefix-to-sibling scan > cwd chain > no flag is
      unchanged, and the existing tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` pass without
      edits to their assertions.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The resolution rule (initialised-only, no
      `.worklog/.worklog` nesting, worktree-ancestor special case) is stated in
      the code docstrings of `_detect_worklog_dir()` / `worklog_dir_flag()` and
      in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (the section that says
      `StatusLifecycle` resolves the worklog dir automatically) and
      `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` (the worklog-store resolution note).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fix lands in this repository.** The defective code is
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` here; `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `skill/`. Do **not** edit another project's `.pi/`, and do not create a
  vendored copy of the helper.
- **Shared seam.** `status_lifecycle` is imported by every skill; keep the
  change narrow (one candidate-selection helper reused by both
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`), with no behaviour change
  for cwds that already resolve correctly.
- **Fail closed, never guess.** Returning no `--worklog-dir` (so `wl` reports
  the real error) is preferred over returning a path that is not an initialised
  store.
- **Hermetic tests.** No real `git worktree`/network in the unit tests;
  `unittest.mock.patch` on `Path.cwd`-derived inputs or `tmp_path` layouts,
  matching the existing test module's style.
- **Gate order.** build → test → commit, never reversed; no ad-hoc `pytest` —
  run tests through the test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- Source of truth: `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (this repo).
- `_detect_worklog_dir()` (line ~258) order: `<cwd>/.worklog` →
  `<git toplevel>/.worklog` → `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`;
  the last two gates call `is_dir()` only, never `_is_initialized_worklog()`.
- `worklog_dir_flag()` (line ~391) has a **second, different** ancestor walk
  that *does* check `_is_initialized_worklog()`, then falls back to
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` — so the two walks disagree.
- Reproduced (Tableau-Card-Engine checkout, registered worktree, git toplevel =
  the worktree):
  ```
  cwd=/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>   (historical reproduction in a sibling project)
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> /home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '…/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog']
  ```
  The stale `…/.worklog/.worklog/` exists and contains only a `worktrees/`
  subdirectory (no `initialized` marker, no `worklog.db`).
- Reproduced (this repository, registered worktree, run from a **subdirectory**
  so the `cwd/.worklog` branch is skipped):
  ```
  cwd=…/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>/skill
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> <that worktree>/.worklog      # config.yaml only — NOT initialised
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '<worktree>/.worklog']
  ```
  i.e. a second manifestation of the same defect (uninitialised candidate),
  at the worktree **root** even though the initialised main store is a direct
  ancestor. Both are in scope via AC1–AC3.
- `_resolve_repo_root()` already handles the worktree case for the framework
  root (`skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py::TestFrameworkRootDerivation`)
  — the framework root is correct; only the *store* resolution is wrong.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` covers prefix scan,
  `resolve_worklog_dir`, `resolve_worklog_flags` precedence and `run_wl`
  injection, but has **no** ancestor-walk / worktree-layout test.
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` re-uses `worklog_dir_flag()`, so it is fixed
  transitively. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` resolves its own target
  project root and is unaffected.
- Adjacent same-class defect, **filed separately** by producer decision as
  `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` (see *Related work*):
  `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (line
  ~48) duplicates the ancestor walk with the same `parent/".worklog"`
  construction and no initialisation check, so `code_freeze_marker_path()`
  would read `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json` from a worktree.

## Desired change

1. Introduce one candidate-selection helper used by both
   `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`:
   - for each ancestor, if the ancestor **is** a worklog directory
     (`name == ".worklog"`), the candidate is that ancestor itself; otherwise
     the candidate is `ancestor / ".worklog"`;
   - only accept a candidate when `_is_initialized_worklog(candidate)` is true
     (in the `_detect_worklog_dir` gate; `worklog_dir_flag` keeps its existing
     "no flag" contract when nothing initialised is found).
2. Delete the duplicated walk in `worklog_dir_flag()` in favour of the shared
   helper (no second, divergent rule).
3. Tests per AC4, in the existing
   `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` module style.
4. Doc updates per AC6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 258)
  gains the `.worklog`-named-ancestor rule and the `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  gate; `worklog_dir_flag()` (~line 391) re-uses the same helper instead of its
  own walk; docstrings per AC6.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` — new
  `TestWorklogDirAncestorWalk` class with the AC4 cases.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — the "`StatusLifecycle` resolves the same
  directory automatically" paragraph (~lines 84–88) gains the initialised-only /
  no-nesting rule.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — worklog-store resolution note
  (~lines 360–364).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` (open, intake_complete) — *implement.py finish reports
  status changes that the main worklog store does not show*. Same seam, wider
  scope (finish must pass an explicit store). Its "Existing state" note claims
  `worklog_dir_flag` "does resolve the main checkout store from a worktree";
  the evidence above shows that holds only when no stale
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` exists — this item carries the counter-example.
  Partial overlap only, so **not** a duplicate.
- `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` — `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's
  non-initialised `.worklog` (the same walk duplicated in `code_freeze.py`).
  Filed separately by producer decision (Appendix Q2) and **blocked by** this
  item, so the shared rule lands first.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — original discovery work item.
- `CG-0MUC5GVCJ0062BN7` (Tableau-Card-Engine, completed) — earlier
  worktree-resolution defect (`.pi/test-config.json` unseen from a worktree):
  same failure family, different file.
- `SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51`, `SA-0MSGH55OJ003WKYZ`, `SA-0MTOMCML900254CI`
  (completed) — the prefix-to-sibling seam and cwd-independence lineage this
  item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: resolver regression elsewhere.** Other skills rely on
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` returning a non-initialised directory in exotic
  layouts. Mitigation: AC5 requires the existing suite to pass unchanged; the
  change only *narrows* accepted candidates, and `worklog_dir_flag()` keeps its
  "no flag" fallback so `wl` still reports its own error.
- **Risk: `.worklog`-named ancestor inside a normal project** (e.g. a directory
  literally called `.worklog` used for something else). Mitigation: the
  `.worklog`-named ancestor is only accepted when `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  is true.
- **Risk: styling split between the two walks** if only one is fixed.
  Mitigation: single shared helper (Desired change 1–2).
- **Scope-creep risk: fixing `code_freeze.py` in the same change.** Excluded by
  producer decision (Appendix Q2) — it is filed separately.
- **Assumption:** the "stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`" directory is a local
  artefact (from an old run) and is not committed anywhere; the fix must not
  depend on its removal, because the nesting rule is wrong regardless.
- **Assumption:** unit tests can express the layout with `tmp_path` +
  `mock.patch` rather than creating real git worktrees (the existing module
  already models the framework-root worktree layout this way).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where should the fix and its record land?** The defective code lives
  in SorraAgents (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`); the TCE checkout has no
  `skill/` tree, so a TCE `implement.py` worktree could not carry the change
  (the TCE-side `implement.py finish` fails closed on out-of-worktree edits).
  Options were: (a) transfer the item to the SA store; (b) create an SA item
  carrying code + tests, keep the CG item as a linked discovery record;
  (c) commit to SorraAgents `dev` from outside a worktree (breaks
  worktree-isolation). Agent recommendation: (b).
  **Answer (producer):** *"SA create there then delete this item"* — create the
  SA item with the full brief (this item) **and delete** the CG item, i.e. a
  transfer rather than a linked pair. Source: operator reply in the intake
  session `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`.
- **Q2 — Fold in the adjacent `code_freeze.py` defect?** Options: (a) fix both
  in this change via one shared helper; (b) keep this item narrow and file the
  `code_freeze` fix as a separate `discovered-from` item. Agent recommendation:
  (b).
  **Answer (producer):** *"file separately"* — the `code_freeze.py`
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` duplicate-walk fix is filed as its own item; this item
  stays narrow. Source: operator reply in the intake session
  `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`.
- **Q3 — Duplicate-work check (agent-resolved).** Searched both stores
  (`worklog_dir_flag`, `worktree resolution`, `nested worklog dir`) —
  `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` is the only overlapping item and its ACs do not cover
  the nesting/initialisation defects, so no duplicate close or rewrite was
  applied; it is cross-referenced in *Related work*. Answer: **no full
  duplicate; partial overlap cross-linked.**

## Goal

One-off operational sweep of the stale `<id>.pending-screens.json` signals left behind by the broken in-main-slot resume cycle fixed in SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S, so the affected items stop being constrained by a gate that can no longer clear.

Discovered-from: SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (audit comment 2026-10-29, "Adjacent scope note 2"). Becomes actionable once the D1/D2 resume fixes land.

## Known backlog (as recorded on 2026-10-29)

| Item | Children pending | Signal written |
|---|---|---|
| LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI | 2 | 2026-10-15 |
| LP-0MVB8F5ZU0079DE9 | 1 | 2026-10-20 |
| LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 | 1 | 2026-10-18 |
| LP-0MVGT0E6W000Q8CY | 3 | 2026-10-23 |
| LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 | 2 | 2026-10-29 |
| LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X | 3 | 2026-10-29 |
| LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG | 6 | 2026-10-29 |

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Enumerate every `<id>.pending-screens.json` under the `llm` project's `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/` and reconcile the list against the table above (record additions/removals in a comment).
- AC2: For each remaining signal, run the parent audit once with the fix in place; where the child audits are already serviced the signal is cleared automatically, otherwise run a forced `--no-child-in-main-slot` audit so the child screens are executed by the runner instead of being emitted for an absent interactive session.
- AC3: Each affected item's audit state is recorded (report verdict + whether the signal is gone); no signal remains for an item whose children are all audited.
- AC4: The sweep does not change verdicts by hand — `wl audit-set` is never used directly; only real runner audits persist reports.

## Minimal implementation

- Shell loop over the checkpoint dir listing, then per item `python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue <id> --no-child-in-main-slot --force` (or the default mode where a fresh serviced child audit exists).

## Migrated from AH-0MWGSW7TM003DXBZ (AI_Hell worklog)

Test child of SA-0MWGZ86MS005OE61 (implement.py drive: spawn-failed child
trips the worktree-placement guard). Originally tracked as
AH-0MWGSW7TM003DXBZ.

discovered-from:AH-0MWFHLDAS008YG0P

## Problem

When a driven child spawns but dies before writing anything (spawn-failed),
its worktree exists but is clean (`has_changes=False`,
`worktree_verdict=CHILD_CLEAN`). The next `phase_parent`/`drive` run then
calls `_child_main_checkout_violation()` which scans the main checkout and
sibling worktrees. If those surfaces are dirty (unrelated to the
spawn-failed child), the violation fires incorrectly, blaming the spawn-failed
child for dirt it never produced.

## User Story

As a driver running `implement.py drive` on an epic, I want spawn-failed
children to be resettable without the placement guard incorrectly blaming
them for unrelated dirt in the main checkout or sibling worktrees.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A spawn-failed child (worktree exists, no changes, no commits ahead) is
  treated as startable-again/reset, not as a placement violation, so the next
  `drive` re-spawns it without requiring manual `abort`.
- The placement guard distinguishes 'this child wrote elsewhere' from 'this
  child wrote nothing and other surfaces happen to be dirty' — the latter must
  not fail the chain.
- Regression test: a spawn-failed child plus a dirty main checkout and a dirty
  sibling worktree does not produce a `_child_main_checkout_violation`; a
  child that genuinely wrote only into a sibling worktree still does.
- No weakening of the genuine cross-worktree-write detection
  (SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I) — existing tests in
  `test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` must continue to pass.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_child_main_checkout_violation`
  call sites in `phase_parent`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — existing
  sibling stray tests, add the spawn-fail regression

## Tests

1. Spawn-failed child + dirty main checkout + dirty sibling worktree → no
   violation, drive continues (not blocked)
2. Spawn-failed child + clean surfaces → reported for re-implementation (happy
   path unchanged)
3. Genuine cross-worktree write → violation still detected (existing test must
   pass — no weakening)
4. Both `skip-in-progress` and `implement` call paths in `phase_parent`
   covered by tests

## Impact

A spawn-failed child no longer trips the placement guard on unrelated dirt: the next run reports it startable again and re-spawns it, so recovering needs no manual `implement.py abort`.
data.title: Test: spawn-failed child with dirty main/sibling is not a placement violation
